recipes.name: Green Bean Casserole
ingredients_raw: 2 (15 ounce) cans cut green beans, drained
1 (10.5 ounce) can condensed cream of mushroom soup

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Mix green beans, condensed cream of mushroom soup, milk, and half of the fried onions together in a 1.5-quart casserole dish.
Bake in the preheated oven until bubbly, about 25 minutes.
Sprinkle remaining onions on top; return to the oven for 5 minutes. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Let rest for a few minutes before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Green Bean Casserole
raw_recipe.description: This green bean casserole recipe uses canned green beans, condensed mushroom soup, and crispy French-fried onions to create a classic holiday favorite.

review.reviewBody: I am giving this a 5 because after lots of changes, this was incredible! I used fench cut beans, 1/2 sour cream instead of all milk, 1/2 cup chopped oinion, and a cup of cheddar cheese. I did not mix any french fried onions in, as they tend to get soggy, I just topped with them (cheddar flavored) instead. My husband who eats NO veggies, and everyone else too, had 2 seving each, our family of four almost polished off this whole casserole. I am very excited, as I have been looking for a green bean casserole recipe, and this was so tasty. Definitely cut down the liquid, or it will be too runny!

Mix the cream of mushroom with the milk, then add pinch of salt, pinch of pepper, 3/4 tsp garlic powder, and 1/2 tsp of onion powder... add green beans and french's fried onions according to recipe... bake 30 mins then add onions on top and 10 more mins. Eliminates wateriness and lack of flavor. I made it this way and didn't have leftovers!!! Almost upsetting until I remembered that meant my guests loved it.

This recipe proves that green beans can indeed be comfort food. My husband and his friends go nuts over these and ask for seconds and thirds. (Vegetables!!) It's now expected that I serve up a pan of this with any special dinner. I used 1/2 cup milk (all you need; makes it super creamy instead of runny) use frozen green beans (4 cups; better texture!! Just bake until tender) ANd ther is NO NEED TO ADD EXTRA SALT- esp. if using canned beans. The soup is salty, the onions are salty, enough already! I also add lots of fresh cracked black pepper.

my meat-only husband actually showed me this recipe. With a few modifications, we eat this every week! I don't like mushy veggies, so I use 1pound cut up fresh green beans. Bring some water to boil and then throw in the beans. Boil them for approximately 5 minutes (or until slightly softened and still a tad crispy) then drain them and throw them into the recipe. In addition to the recipe, we add garlic powder (approx 1tablespoon) and sometimes a bit of onion powder. OMG to die for!

I have made this a few times. Honestly, it's a little bland as it's posted here. I use cream of celery soup, french onion dip in place of the milk, a fair amount of ground black pepper, a pinch of cayenne, and I bake it for about 30 minutes at 375 before taking it out to put the fried onions on top, then return to the oven for at least 5 more minutes. This thickens up the soupiness a little more and makes it feel more like a casserole! It's always the first thing that's empty now whenever I make it! Highly recommended!!

I use 3 cans of beans instead of 2. I also add shredded cheese and 1/2 teaspoon of garlic powder and 1/2 teaspoon of onion powder. The extra beans makes this recipe perfect and it is not too liquidy at all!! My family loves this at every holiday and they say it beats every other green bean casserole. I always double the recipe so in that case I use 6 cans of beans and double everything else. I always use a large foil disposable casserole pan for easy cleaning!!

Awesome! We always add extra French fried onions. I usually bake this in the oven, but did it in the crock pot on Thanksgiving. It worked great! It was a bit soupy once it got hot so we just tipped the lid on the pot for a couple of hours. Next time we use the crock pot, we would add less milk. Since this method of cooking wouldn't result in crispy onions on top, we simply toasted some French fried onions in the oven for a few minutes and served them on the side. Everyone loved it!

Personally I prefer fresh green beans as opposed to canned or frozen. It is so much better tasting. Of course you do have to process the green beans, clean, trim, cut and cook prior to making the casserole.

I made a double batch, reduced the milk, added French onion dip, some worschchire sauce, some garlic and onion powder, 4 oz of baby bella sliced mushrooms and it was TREMENDOUS!! Savory flavor and a perfect side dish. Flavor profile is MUCH better than the standard. Added an extra can of green beans, too. Voila!!

A family favorite! I use half and half instead of milk, I mix it with the soup in a bowl first so it's well incorporated then I add frozen green beans that I've partially thawed, the onions and bacon bits. One year I had extra bacon bits and threw those in, bacon is now a must add.
I replaced the cream of mushroom with cream of fennel and it was great. I was out of green beans, so I used white beans. My husband hates onions so I sprinkled La Choy chow mein noodles!

I've been making this recipe for years. I followed the recipe but added about two teaspoons of Worcester sauce and 12 ounces of fresh mushrooms. It is a great variation for this recipe. It is the same recipe my mom used over 50 years ago.
Really simple and delish. On my send one I cooked i added just a touch of worshtishire sauce. Yummy!!
We make this every holiday; it's one of our easiest family favorites and there is never any leftovers when it comes to this dish.

Everything is what I normally do. I didn't know about the soy sauce or the last 5min to top it off with the remaining fried onions . I've always topped it off at the beginning of cooking. Thank you so much. Everyone loved this recipe better than I've normally have done. Easy pleasy. Thank you again.
Simple, delicious. The only change was the addition of a few portobello mushrooms.
Use a little less milk if you want to double the recipe!

I made this for Christmas dinner and it was delicious. I'm glad I have leftovers. I will eat a plate of this as a meal. You should try this , it's easy to prepare. I did make a couple of changes though. First, I used French cut style green beans, only because they are my husband's favorite. And I baked them in a 9"x 9" pan. So Yummy!!!
I love this recipe and so did the family I went to make my ol mans plate and be time I turned around it was all gone
